newsitem.title: UK: Consumer recovery boosts Kingfisher profit.
newsitem.headline: Consumer recovery boosts Kingfisher profit.

text.p: British retailer Kingfisher Plc on Wednesday reported a 47 percent increase in half year profits, driven by a strong recovery at its home decorating business B&Q.

Pretax profits for the half year to August 3 rose to 109.6 million pounds ($170.3 million) from 74.6 million, on retail sales up 10.4 percent to 2.50 billion pounds from 2.27 billion. The dividend was up 11 percent to 5.0 pence a share.
At B&Q, the market leader in home improvement retailing, profits rebounded 48 percent to 47.0 million pounds from 31.8 million and sales were up nearly 16 percent.
Chief executive Sir Geoffrey Mulcahy said, "This was an encouraging six months for Kingfisher."
He said in a statement the figures were in line or ahead of the company's targets and reflected operational improvements as well as the upturn in consumer confidence in some of its markets.

Woolworths bounced back into profit of 4.6 million pounds after a loss last year of 900,000. Comet, the electricals retailer reduced its first half loss to three million pounds from 8.7 million last time. ($1=.6436 Pound)
